record.original_question: Suppose q_1, ..., q_m : F2^n -> F2 are degree-at-most-2 polynomials and the indicator of the all-ones vector, namely AND : F2^n -> {-1,1}, can be written as AND(x) = sum_{i=1}^m c_i (-1)^{q_i(x)} for real coefficients c_i. What lower bound on m is necessary?

evidence.quote: Statement: Suppose q_1, ..., q_m : F2^n -> F2 are polynomials of degree at most 2 and suppose the indicator function of (1, ..., 1) in F2^n, namely AND : F2^n -> {-1, 1}, is expressible as AND( x) = sum_{i=1}^m c_i (-1)^{q_i(x)} for some real numbers c_i. What is a lower bound for m?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ be an integer and identify $\mathbb{F}_2 = \{0,1\}$. Define the AND function $\mathrm{AND} : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \{-1, 1\}$ by
$$\mathrm{AND}(x) = \begin{cases} -1 & \text{if } x = (1,1,\dots,1), \\ 1 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$
Suppose there exist polynomials $q_1, \dots, q_m : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$, each of total degree at most $2$ (when written as a multilinear polynomial in the coordinates $x_1, \dots, x_n$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$), and real numbers $c_1, \dots, c_m \in \mathbb{R}$ such that for every $x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$,
$$\mathrm{AND}(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{m} c_i \, (-1)^{q_i(x)}.$$
Determine the best possible (largest) lower bound on $m$ as a function of $n$. In particular, is it true that $m \geq 2^{\Omega(n)}$ is necessary?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in Ryan O'Donnell's compilation of open problems in analysis of Boolean functions (sourced from Hamed Hatami, 2011). It is recorded as open: Hatami can show $m \geq n$ is necessary and conjectures $m \geq 2^{\Omega(n)}$. The degree-1 case is fully resolved with $m = 2^n$. No subsequent resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Real Analysis in Computer Science: A Collection of Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Hamed Hatami can show that m ≥ n is necessary but conjectures m ≥ 2^Ω(n) is necessary. If the qᵢ's are of degree at most 1, then m = 2ⁿ is necessary and sufficient.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem with only a linear lower bound known and an exponential lower bound conjectured.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Analysis of Boolean Functions (arXiv:1204.6447)
status_evidence.snippet: A list of open problems in the field of analysis of boolean functions, compiled February 2012 for the Simons Symposium.
status_evidence.claim: The question appears in a curated list of open problems in Boolean function analysis.
